claims.statement: Allocation rule v18 (east-first multi-node reservation) went live at 22:00 and correlates temporally with the 06:00 pickup failure onset
claims.corroboration: m8_e02 shows east-node specific >90min hold at 06:00; no release notes (m8_e04) list other allocation changes
claims.limitation: temporal correlation only; does not establish mechanism

claims.statement: All 186 held orders were routed to east node and flagged as split-reservation exceptions by the allocator
claims.corroboration: m8_e02 confirms isolation to east-node lanes; m8_e01 reports inventory reconciles (no stock shortage)
claims.limitation: single non-authoritative source (tier 2); 'split-reservation exception' semantics unknown without rule inspection

claims.statement: The pattern is discriminating: 100% of held orders are east-node, 100% are split-reservation exceptions, 100% post-rule-change, other nodes unaffected
claims.corroboration: m8_e04 rules out competing releases; m8_e09 notes observability gap but does not contradict
claims.limitation: correlation strong but mechanism (rule defect vs. downstream carrier feed lag) requires diagnostic

capability_gaps.reason: m8_e09 observability gap: dashboards do not show how booked pickups relate to carrier confirmation; cannot distinguish allocation defect from carrier-side lag without seeing carrier state

next_action.rationale: Highest-value diagnostic to discriminate allocation_rule_defect from carrier_feed_lag. Will show whether orders are stuck at allocation→carrier-handoff boundary or within carrier's pickup queue. This is the discriminating test: if split-reservation exceptions fail at handoff, points to rule defect; if they reach carrier and sit there, points to carrier-side lag or dock conflict.
next_action.expected_information_gain: Direct evidence of whether the failure is in allocation rule logic (orders malformed/incomplete at handoff) or downstream (orders valid but carrier not picking up)
